description: Connecticut-only rules checked against the cited statutes and official DMV pages. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Connecticut makes it unlawful to drive faster than 55 mph
options: On every road, including limited-access highways posted at 65
Except on multiple-lane limited-access highways with set limits
questions.explanation: Section 14-219(a)(2) prohibits a speed greater than 55 miles per hour on a highway other than a highway specified in section 14-218a(b)(1) for which a speed limit has been established under that subdivision.

questions.q: On a multiple-lane limited-access highway for which Connecticut has established a speed limit under section 14-218a(b)(1), it is unlawful to drive faster than
questions.explanation: Section 14-219(a)(3) prohibits a speed greater than 65 miles per hour on a highway specified in section 14-218a(b)(1) for which a speed limit has been established. Section 14-218a(b)(1) tells the Office of the State Traffic Administration to establish a speed limit not to exceed 65 on each multiple-lane, limited-access highway.

questions.q: A Connecticut local traffic authority generally may not establish or reduce a speed limit lower than
questions.explanation: Section 14-218a says the traffic authority shall not establish or reduce a speed limit lower than 25 miles per hour unless the limit is in a pedestrian safety zone under section 14-307a or the required engineering study finds that a limit lower than 25 is reasonable. Connecticut does not set one statewide urban speed in that section.

questions.q: A Connecticut driver under 18 commits speeding by going more than 20 mph over the limit when that limit is
options: Less than 65 mph and set by statute
Any number, including a 70 mph zone
Posted only in a work zone
questions.explanation: Section 14-219(a)(4) applies that under-18 rule on a highway or road for which a speed limit of less than 65 miles per hour has been established under section 14-218a or section 14-307a.

questions.q: Section 14-218a(a) prohibits driving on a Connecticut public highway, or on school property, at a speed
options: Of exactly 25 mph in every town
questions.explanation: Section 14-218a(a)(1) is the reasonable-speed rule and expressly includes school property. It does not set a single numeric school-zone speed. Greater than is reasonable, having regard to width, traffic, use, intersections, and weather.

questions.q: Connecticut's elevated blood alcohol content, for a driver who is not operating a commercial motor vehicle, is
questions.explanation: Section 14-227a defines elevated blood alcohol content as eight-hundredths of one percent or more of alcohol by weight, except that the figure is four-hundredths of one percent or more when the person is operating a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.q: When the person is operating a commercial motor vehicle, Connecticut's elevated blood alcohol content is
questions.explanation: The definition in section 14-227a says that if the person is operating a commercial motor vehicle, elevated blood alcohol content means four-hundredths of one percent or more of alcohol by weight.

questions.q: A person under 21 may not operate a motor vehicle in Connecticut when the ratio of alcohol in the blood is
options: Two-hundredths of one percent or more by weight
0.04 percent only in a commercial vehicle
questions.explanation: Section 14-227g(a) says no person less than twenty-one years of age shall operate a motor vehicle while the ratio of alcohol in the blood is two-hundredths of one percent or more of alcohol, by weight.

questions.q: Connecticut suspends an operator's license for 30 days when a conviction raises the point total
questions.explanation: Regulations of Connecticut State Agencies section 14-137a-8(a) says that when a conviction raises the point total above ten points, the commissioner gives notice of a 30-day suspension. A pre-suspension hearing is limited to identity and whether the licensee accumulated more than ten points within a 24-month period.

questions.q: The legal age for a Connecticut learner's permit and for a driver's license is
questions.explanation: The Connecticut DMV teen-driver page states that the legal age is 16 for both a learner's permit and a driver's license.

questions.q: Connecticut learner's-permit training includes 40 hours of practice driving, and the permit must be held at least
questions.explanation: The DMV driver-training page says the 40 hours of behind-the-wheel practice may be given by any combination of commercial, secondary, or parent instruction. A learner's permit holder may apply for a license after holding the permit at least 120 days on the driving-school path or 180 days for home training.

questions.q: Until the 18th birthday, a Connecticut 16- or 17-year-old licensee may not drive between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m. except for
options: Any trip with a parent texting permission
Work, school, religion, or medical necessity
There is no curfew after the first month
questions.explanation: The DMV restrictions page states the 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. curfew until the 18th birthday with those purposes. It also says passenger and curfew restrictions do not apply to active members of a volunteer fire company or department, volunteer ambulance service, or medical service organization while responding to, returning from, or carrying out emergency duties. Employment, school, religious activities, or medical necessity, and the separate passenger rules still apply.

questions.q: During the first six months, a newly licensed Connecticut 16- or 17-year-old may carry passengers only if they are
questions.explanation: The DMV restrictions page limits the first six months to those passengers. During the second six months, immediate family may also ride. All passengers must use permanently installed seat belts, and until age 18 the driver may not use a cell phone, even hands-free, or another mobile electronic device. A parent or legal guardian, at least one of whom holds a valid license; or a person at least 20 who has held a license for four years with no suspension in those four years. A licensed driving instructor.

questions.q: In Connecticut, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Connecticut requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 4 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Connecticut complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Connecticut requires 40 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: In Connecticut, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Connecticut, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years and 4 months.

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Connecticut not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Connecticut restricts provisional drivers from 11 p.m. to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.

questions.q: In Connecticut, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Connecticut drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 18 years.

provenance.manual: File 131 as amended by Senate "A", "B", and "C")* - Cga.ct.gov

questions.q: How many questions are on the Connecticut car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Connecticut car knowledge test has 25 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Connecticut car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Connecticut car knowledge test.

provenance.manual: File 131 as amended by Senate "A", "B", and "C")* - Cga.ct.gov

questions.q: In Connecticut, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Connecticut sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

questions.q: In Connecticut, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Connecticut brings a suspension of 45 days.

provenance.manual: Driving under the influence (DUI) \| CT DMV

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Connecticut?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Connecticut can be posted up to 65 mph for cars.

questions.q: Which best describes Connecticut's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: Connecticut: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Connecticut?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Connecticut, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.

questions.q: How is Connecticut's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
No seat belt law for adults
questions.explanation: Connecticut seat belt enforcement is primary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Connecticut?
questions.explanation: Connecticut requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.

questions.q: What is Connecticut's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Connecticut requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $25,000.
